grade.first_issue: The first decisive defect is the false claim that every inclusion-minimal hitting set of \(\mathcal F_n\) has size at most \(|Q_1|\). For the admissible start \(a_1=35\), the greedy sequence begins \(35,40,42,45\), with supports \(\{5,7\},\{2,5\},\{2,3,7\},\{3,5\}\). Then \(\{2,3,7\}\) is a minimal hitting set of size 3, whereas \(|Q_1|=2\). Thus the claimed bound, and likewise the asserted product bound by \(\prod_{p\in Q_1}p\), is false.
grade.summary: The hitting-set reformulation is useful, and the proof correctly shows that the least product among minimal hitting sets is nondecreasing and bounded. However, this gives no control over all of \(M_n\). The conclusion that the entire set \(M_n\) stabilizes is unsupported and rests on a false bound; proving the necessary global finiteness/stabilization is the central difficulty. Hence Rule E caps the score at 3, below Rule C's cap for the initial false load-bearing assertion. Moreover, the final backward induction is invalid: for \(m\le i<m-1+T'\), it uses \(a_i=a_{i-T'}+L'\), although the induction hypothesis permits this only when \(i-T'\ge m\), and some such indices are not even positive. Thus the proof establishes at most a conditional eventual translation law and does not handle the required initial range, also invoking Rule D.
strengths: Correctly reformulates admissibility using prime-support hitting sets.
Correctly proves that the minimum element of \(M_n\) is nondecreasing and bounded.
Conditional on stabilization of \(M_n\), correctly observes the translation equivariance \(g(a+L)=g(a)+L\) and obtains an eventual translation period from finite-state dynamics.

errors.description: The asserted cardinality bound for arbitrary minimal hitting sets is false, even for prime-support families arising from an admissible greedy sequence.

Stabilization of the whole family \(M_n\) does not follow from stabilization of its minimum. The claim \(mp\le\prod_{p\in Q_1}p\) is unjustified, and new primes and large minimal hitting sets are not controlled. This is an unsupported central structural inference under Rule E.

The backward induction applies the eventual translation identity outside its quantified range, so \(a_{m-1}+L'\) is not shown to share a factor with all preceding terms. The extension from eventual periodicity to every positive index therefore fails under Rule D.
